name: srl
description: Buildless reactive frontend library, its component collection, its toolchain, and the example application

scripts.check: npm run typecheck && npm run templates:check && npm run lint && npm run test:tools && npm run vendor && npm run package && npm run verify && npm run docs:check && npm run docs:adr && npm run test

//layout: source/             the library, and a package of its own: source/package.json
declares what it publishes. Extracting it is a file move.
source/dist/        the four bundles `npm run package` emits for the registry
consumer. Generated, ignored, rebuilt by `npm run check`.
source/lib/         the framework: core, auth, host, its vendored runtime
dependencies and its own tests. Depends on nothing here.
source/components/  reusable prebundled components built on source/lib.
example/            an application. Any root directory with an index.html is
one; the tools discover them rather than being told.
A browser sees three mounts on one origin: / for the application, /lib/ for
source/lib, /components/ for source/components. The library declares the two
that are its own in source/package.json, tools/package/interface.mjs reads
them, and everything else asks there: tools/dev/serve.mjs and
web-test-runner.config.mjs import it, the delivery tooling asks for it through
tools/layout.mjs (--deploy-pairs), and each application's index.html pastes
the generated fragment, source/lib/importmap.json.
tools/layout.mjs holds what is true of this repository and not of the library:
where the package sits, and which directories are applications.
Every script takes `--app <dir>` (or APP=<dir> for the test runner). There is
no default application: with two in the repository, a tool that picks one
builds or deploys the wrong thing sooner or later.
npm start                             serve example (the flag is in the script)
npm run serve -- --app <name>         serve another application
APP=example npm test                  lib suite + that application's suite
npm run importmap                     regenerate the published import map
npm run package                       the four bundles source/package.json exports
npm run build -- --app example        verified artifact for one application
//running-it: `npm start` is a convenience, not a requirement. It runs tools/dev/serve.mjs,
which is plain Node with zero dependencies, so it works from a fresh clone
with no npm install. Every runtime dependency the browser needs is committed:
source/lib/vendor holds all three. The one thing a clone does not come with is
<app>/app.css, the compiled stylesheet, because it is generated rather than
written; index.html loads the Tailwind browser JIT instead, and a deployment
that wants the compiled file runs `npm run css` (which does need npm install).
node tools/dev/serve.mjs              static server, history fallback, watch
python3 -m http.server                needs the /lib mount, so it does not
work here any more: two directories on
one origin is the one thing a bare file
//devDependencies: NOTHING HERE IS SHIPPED, AND NOTHING HERE IS NEEDED TO RUN THE APP. The
browser gets every runtime dependency from source/lib/vendor, of which there
are three: lit, @preact/signals-core and (development only)
@tailwindcss/browser. They are committed files, integrity-pinned in every
application's index.html, and re-fetched only by `npm run vendor`.
node_modules exists so that tsc, eslint and the test runner can resolve types
for the same versions source/lib/vendor serves. tools/checks/verify-deps.mjs fails the
build if the two drift apart.
Every vendored package is pinned exactly, with no caret, because a range
would let npm install types for a version /vendor does not contain — and,
since `npm run vendor` copies each notice out of the LICENSE npm installed,
a notice for one either. @tailwindcss/browser is declared for that second
reason alone: nothing imports it and tsc never types it, but its notice
ships in source/lib/vendor/LICENSES.md and has to be checked against
something. tools/checks/verify-deps.mjs reads the list from
source/lib/vendor/provenance.json rather than repeating it here.
Two TypeScript installs, on purpose:
typescript@6.0.3  - has the compiler API, which typescript-eslint's
type-aware rules require (peer range >=4.8.4 <6.1.0).
tsgo -> typescript@7.0.2 - the Go-native compiler, ~10x faster, used for
`npm run typecheck`. It ships no public compiler API
until 7.1, so it cannot back typescript-eslint yet.
Same tsconfig, same semantics (7.0 is a port, not a rewrite). Invoked by
path because both packages claim the `tsc` bin name.
puppeteer-core and chrome-launcher are declared because tools/benchmark imports
them directly: the harness drives Chrome over the DevTools protocol to collect
garbage and read a heap, which no test-runner plugin exposes. Both also arrive
as transitive dependencies of @web/test-runner-chrome, and leaving them
undeclared would make the benchmark break the day that package stopped
depending on them. Pinned exactly, at the versions already installed.
